candidate_methods.name: Raise the roadway profile (raised roadway barrier)
candidate_methods.summary: Raise the road (and usually sidewalks) so the road itself acts as a flood barrier and/or stays above design flood elevation.

screening.check: Building setbacks from back of sidewalk
Surveyed road elevation with vertical datum

sourced_points.text: The guideline sample considers raised roadways with a 4-ft grade change, and notes the approach may also apply to elevating emergency evacuation routes.
Option 1 (retaining walls and/or slopes) may be feasible where buildings are set back at least 14 ft from the back of sidewalk.
The guidelines do not recommend a raised roadway barrier where existing buildings sit at the back of sidewalk; raising only the roadway creates safety, drainage, ADA and access impacts.
Once a street is raised, a stormwater pump system (pumps, generators) adds ongoing O&M cost; the guideline expects stormwater costs to be significant, citing Miami Beach raised-road projects.

hypotheses: Raising one corridor does not by itself block flood pathways that enter around its ends or through adjacent low ground.
failure_modes: Flanking around the ends of the raised section
Ponding behind the raised road without pumped drainage
required_data: Surveyed road and adjacent grade elevations with vertical datum
candidate_methods.cause_gate: Only relevant if coastal_overland is confirmed; currently possible.

candidate_methods.name: Vegetated berm / landscaped embankment along the flood side
candidate_methods.summary: An earthen, planted embankment with crest and access paths placed between the water and the road.

screening.check: Open space between road and water for a berm footprint
Surveyed road elevation with vertical datum

sourced_points.text: The guideline sample berm extends about 2,000 ft with an assumed grade change of about 2 ft for 2030 design flood elevation (DFE) conditions, with an incremental 2070 raise considered.
The sample design drawings tabulate crest, slope, and access-path widths by height, so a berm needs a horizontal footprint that grows with height.
The Morrissey study's key findings say coastal resilience measures should focus on nature-based solutions.

hypotheses: A berm only protects the road if it ties into high ground at both ends; otherwise water can route around it.
failure_modes: Seepage through or under the embankment
required_data: Available open space and ownership on the flood side
Topography (LiDAR is a start, survey needed)
candidate_methods.cause_gate: Only relevant if coastal_overland is confirmed; currently possible.

candidate_methods.name: Strengthen alternate access routes
candidate_methods.summary: Rather than protecting this corridor, investigate whether improving a detour route preserves the same journeys.

screening.check: Flood exposure of the detour route

sourced_points.text: Whether a detour exists, and how long it is, comes from the network analysis for this corridor (see network impact).
Network results report a detour for journeys j-fx-01, j-fx-03; disconnected: j-fx-02.

hypotheses: A detour is only useful if it is itself outside the flood scenario footprint and has capacity for diverted traffic.
failure_modes: Detour floods in the same scenario
Detour lacks capacity or emergency-vehicle suitability
required_data: Flood exposure of the detour roads
candidate_methods.cause_gate: Network/access measure; does not address a flooding cause.

candidate_methods.name: Deployable (temporary) flood barrier
candidate_methods.summary: Barriers deployed before or during a flood and retracted afterward; may be an interim measure.

screening.check: Agency that would store and deploy the barrier

sourced_points.text: The guideline defines deployable barriers as systems deployed before and/or during a flood event and retracted afterward, and lists types from pre-installed and passive systems to mobile units and water-filled tubes.
The guideline presents a comparison matrix rather than a sample site; product mentions are not endorsements.

hypotheses: Deployment depends on forecast lead time, trained crews, storage, and access; a barrier placed across a road closes that road while deployed.
failure_modes: Seepage at joints or under the base
Blocks the road it is meant to protect while deployed
required_data: Warning time available for the relevant flood type
candidate_methods.cause_gate: Only relevant if coastal_overland is confirmed; currently possible.

other_methods_considered.name: Drainage, backflow prevention, and stormwater storage
other_methods_considered.reason: Passed screening but outside the top 4 offered.

details.name: Drainage, backflow prevention, and stormwater storage
details.summary: Address water that enters through or ponds on the road via the drainage system (tide gates/check valves, inlet capacity, storage, pumping).

sourced_points.text: The Morrissey study notes stormwater flooding may be a significant problem in the Central section because there is limited gravity to discharge stormwater at high tide.
The Morrissey study evaluated tide-gate options (including No Tide Gate and Hybrid) combined with raising the basin-side beach/dune/berm and a bay-side barrier.

hypotheses: Drainage works alone do not stop coastal surge from overtopping a road; they address rainfall and backflow pathways.
failure_modes: Mismatch between rainfall and surge drivers
required_data: Rainfall vs surge contribution to the documented flooding
details.cause_gate: Only relevant if tidal_outfall_backwater or storm_drain_capacity is confirmed; currently possible, unresolved.

caveats: These are conceptual 'opinion of probable cost' figures for sample barriers at sample sites in the City of Boston guidelines published October 2018. They are not bids, not 2026 prices, and not transferable per-foot rates for another site.
Escalation from the 2018 publication date to today is not applied here. Any escalation index and base year must be chosen by a cost estimator.
The guidelines state each opinion reflects sample design considerations and does not reflect engineering analyses prepared for design.
estimating_method_guidance: Treat the sample $/100-LF as an order-of-magnitude reference only; site length, grade change, setbacks, utilities and foundations drive the real number.

A preliminary estimate for this corridor would start from surveyed length and required grade change, quantity take-offs per line item, current local unit prices, escalation from the price base year, and explicitly priced exclusions (pumps, utilities, permitting).
Present any scaled number as 'illustrative scaling of a 2018 sample', never as a project cost.

site_specific_estimate.note: Site cost estimation is a separate engineering task.

local_precedents.text: Present-day flood pathways into the study area were identified at Tenean Beach/Conley Street, southeast of Kosciuszko Circle, Bianculli Boulevard, Pattens Cove, and Quincy Shore Drive/Neponset Trail; in a 2030 extreme event these expand and new pathways appear from Moakley Park and the I-93 underpass.
The study notes flood protection is being advanced outside the central section (Bianculli Boulevard to Freeport Street), leaving that area as a key storm-surge pathway into the study area.
The study records that DCR's 2017 Morrissey Boulevard redesign planned to elevate the roadway for coastal resiliency, with a stated target of limiting tidal-flooding closures to fewer than 3 in 2065.

Stormwater flooding may remain a significant problem in the Central section because of limited gravity discharge at high tide; one option assumes BWSC's proposed additional stormwater infrastructure for the Northern section.

Key findings state flood mitigation could be implemented along the coastline and Dorchester Bay Basin, should focus on nature-based solutions, and that environmental permitting is expected to be complex.
Infrastructure in the area is owned by multiple jurisdictions (including MassDOT, DCR, MBTA, City of Boston, utilities, and private owners), so any project needs coordinated ownership and permitting.

cause_assessment.finding: Flooding on this corridor is documented or modelled, and drainage complaints are reported nearby. The cause is not established. possible_causes.label: High tide blocking stormwater discharge / backflow
possible_causes.description: When the receiving water is high, outfalls cannot drain by gravity; stormwater backs up through the drain system and ponds on the street.
unknowns: Which outfall(s) serve the corridor inlets and who owns them
Outfall invert elevations vs tide levels (datum)
Whether tide gates / check valves exist and work
Timing of past flooding vs tide and rainfall
possible_causes.does_not_prove: High tide alone does not show that a specific outfall is failing.
possible_causes.status_basis: Evidence is consistent with this cause but does not establish it.

possible_causes.label: Localized inlet obstruction / debris
possible_causes.description: Catch basins or grates are blocked by debris, sediment, leaves or snow so water cannot enter the drain.
unknowns: Current condition of the corridor catch basins
Whether reported ponding cleared after cleaning
Not represented in the BWSC Inundation Model (see ev-bwsc-model-scope).
possible_causes.does_not_prove: A 311 report is an allegation, not a confirmed blockage; the BWSC model does not represent individual clogged basins.
possible_causes.status_basis: Evidence is consistent with this cause but does not establish it.

possible_causes.label: Insufficient storm-drain or inlet capacity
possible_causes.description: Inlets or pipes cannot carry the rainfall runoff reaching them even when clear.
unknowns: Design storm used for the existing system
Not represented in the BWSC Inundation Model (see ev-bwsc-model-scope).
possible_causes.does_not_prove: Road width or a flood footprint does not reveal underground capacity.

possible_causes.label: Unfavorable street grading / ponding
possible_causes.description: Surface low points or grades direct runoff to places without adequate inlets.
unknowns: Validated surface elevations along the corridor (from Person 2 / survey)
Inlet positions relative to low points
possible_causes.does_not_prove: A low point alone does not prove deficient drainage, and regrading can push water elsewhere.

possible_causes.label: Multiple simultaneous causes / unresolved
possible_causes.description: Rain, tide and coastal inflow may combine, or available evidence does not discriminate between causes.
unknowns: Owner records for all drainage assets
possible_causes.does_not_prove: Never force one causal label just to populate an answer.
possible_causes.status_basis: 3 mechanisms have some supporting evidence; the evidence does not discriminate between them.

assets_to_investigate.location_ref: Pipes connecting corridor inlets to their outfall (not public)
Outfall(s) serving the corridor inlets: not identified
Central section shoreline pathway, Bianculli Blvd to Freeport St (per S12)

cause_assessment.assets_note: 10 nearest of 59 mapped catch basins listed.
cause_assessment.owner_note: Owner codes for nearby mapped catch basins: DCR 47, PRIV 10, BWSC 2. Send maintenance requests to the confirmed owner; do not assume BWSC.

cause_matched_actions.name: Survey the shoreline edge and suspected entry pathway
cause_matched_actions.applicable_if: Coastal flood extent or documented pathway reaches the corridor.
cause_matched_actions.could_fail: Survey misses a pathway that only activates at higher water levels.
downstream_checks: Confirm pathway against historical high-water marks (USGS 2018) where available

cause_matched_actions.name: Trace corridor inlets to their outfall(s) and confirm owner
cause_matched_actions.applicable_if: Always, before any outfall or tide-gate proposal.
cause_matched_actions.could_fail: Records incomplete; non-Commission outfalls are outside the BWSC model.
downstream_checks: Request drainage plans from the identified owner

cause_matched_actions.name: Compare reported flooding dates against tide and rainfall records
cause_matched_actions.applicable_if: Dated flood reports exist for the corridor.
cause_matched_actions.could_fail: Report dates are case-open times, not flood times; rainfall gauge may be distant.
downstream_checks: NOAA tide gauge 8443970 for water level; NOAA Atlas 14 for rainfall frequency context

cause_matched_actions.name: Inspect and, if blocked, clean the corridor catch basins
cause_matched_actions.applicable_if: Catch-basin reports or debris notes near the corridor.
cause_matched_actions.could_fail: Flooding persists after cleaning, pointing to capacity or tide causes instead.
downstream_checks: Record whether ponding recurs after cleaning
Report to the asset owner, not by default to BWSC

cause_matched_actions.name: CCTV the connecting pipe if cleaning does not restore drainage
cause_matched_actions.applicable_if: Basins clean but water still not draining.
cause_matched_actions.could_fail: Defect lies further downstream or at the outfall.
downstream_checks: Follow to the next structure / outfall

cause_matched_actions.name: Convene asset owners and collect drainage records before choosing a measure
cause_matched_actions.applicable_if: Two or more mechanisms are possible or ownership is split.
downstream_checks: Hydraulic modelling once records are assembled

cause_matched_actions.name: Drainage capacity assessment (inlets and pipes) with the owner's records
cause_matched_actions.applicable_if: Ponding recurs with clean inlets during rainfall.
cause_matched_actions.could_fail: Records missing; tailwater (tide) controls rather than pipe size.
downstream_checks: Use practitioner drainage guidance (MassDOT PDDG Ch. 8)
Check impacts away from the site

cause_matched_actions.name: Topographic survey of gutters, low points and inlet positions
cause_matched_actions.applicable_if: Ponding is localized to a repeatable spot.
cause_matched_actions.could_fail: LiDAR resolution insufficient at curb scale.
downstream_checks: Check where redirected water would go

cause_matched_actions.name: Evaluate continuous coastal protection (berm, wall, raised road) only where overland entry is demonstrated
cause_matched_actions.applicable_if: Survey shows overland entry along a definable alignment that ties into high ground.
cause_matched_actions.could_fail: Water enters around the ends; outfalls behind the barrier still back up at high tide (see BWSC adaptation scenarios).
downstream_checks: Check drainage behind the barrier at high tide
cause_matched_actions.gate: Only after checks confirm this mechanism.

cause_matched_actions.name: Review tide gate / backflow control, storage or pumping at the outfall
cause_matched_actions.applicable_if: Outfall is identified and tide-constrained discharge is shown by timing or modelling.
cause_matched_actions.could_fail: Storage or pumping undersized; gate closed during rain with no relief; power failure.
downstream_checks: Upstream ponding when the gate is closed
quote_inputs: Required storage volume or pump rate
cause_matched_actions.gate: Only after checks confirm this mechanism.

intervention_caveats: Do not choose road elevation from flood exposure or network priority alone; it addresses coastal overland inflow only.
Drainage or maintenance actions have no published cost example here: cost_estimate_unavailable until quoted.
2018 barrier/raised-road sample costs apply only to coastal capital options, never to catch-basin cleaning or drainage retrofits.
A drainage fix does not change road exposure, property-loss projections, or network ranking without validated before/after flood analysis.
No avoided property damage is claimed.
limitations: Hypotheses to investigate, not a hydraulic diagnosis.
Statuses are evidence categories, not probabilities.
311 data are resident reports with closure notes; catch basin data are mapped attributes, not condition.
Pipe network, outfall locations, inverts and maintenance logs were not publicly available as data.
